Why are most guns painted black instead of being brightly coloured?
They were originally treated with a bluing compound to prevent rust. Most still are.

Black paint doesn't show scratches, scuffs and dirt as easy. Also, a lot of guns are 'blued' to protect against corrosion. As more polymers are used in guns more bright colors are being used. Pink and green being the most common. Pink for 'women's' guns and green for the zombie hunter crowd.

They arent painted, paint interferes with moving parts and comes off pretty easily. Especially when those surfaces are smooth like metal comes out to be normally, painting a gun requires acid etching or something to rough up the surface for paint to adhere too.

Mainly it goes back to history, historically the best way to preserve a gun against rusting was a treatment called "blue" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluing_(steel) It produces a thin layer of corrosion resistant material on the surface of the gun. Think of it like anodizing aluminum, but much much older and for carbon steel.

Since then we have come up with Parkerization, which is how most military guns seem to be treated today. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkerizing Again, a way to produce a thin layer of corrosion resistant material that is tougher and bonded better than mere paint.

There are other methods, but you get the gist.

Tradition often dictates taste, so most gun owners prefer these classic and tough finishes. (I like parkerization myself) When you add that guns are often for hunting, defense and militia use, you can see why dark colors are the most common.

Others are available, guns in shiny stainless steel, chrome plating, gold plating, and specialized paints of all colors are available, but they are novelties, a niche market.

Why do you ask?

I wouldn't call stainless or chrome plating a niche market. A lot of revolvers come in stainless, and is usually a preferred style for this platform.

Brushed finishes are also available, and also something I wouldn't consider a niche market. Again, it's pretty common for revolvers to come with a brushed finish, like the S&W Airweight.

I agree that it is not a small niche, but if you go to the store most guns are dark colored.

My dad loves shiny guns, we make fun of his taste regularly, asking if he wants some diamonds on it.

Depends on what store you're going to.

The gun store I frequent splits handguns, and the revolver "section" tends to be stainless or chrome of some kind. There's almost never a blued revolver in there.

Pylomer-framed pistols tend to be black, which is strange, but there are also OD green and desert tan frames in polymer. They're more rare, but they're out there.

Hunting rifles and shotguns come in camo-colors, or with stainless barrels and wood stocks, most often. I rarely see fully-bued barrels with black synthetic stocks... Although that's not to say they don't exist.

Usually CC pistols are all black, due to the desire to keep them hidden under clothing. It's easier to see a shiny stainless, or a fluorescent pink, peeking out from under a shirt than, black.

So, the store I go to actually has a smaller percentage of "black guns" than other color choices.
